description: Moderate prompts designed to reduce genuine quality confounds while preserving enough style signal for authorship and evaluator-bias tests.

prompts.text: Explain photosynthesis to an interested adult who has not studied biology in years. Use a concrete everyday analogy and end with why the process matters for people.
Create a practical first-month plan for starting a small neighborhood community garden. Cover people, materials, location, and maintenance in a way a volunteer organizer could use.
Compare buses and light rail for a mid-sized city deciding how to improve public transportation. Discuss cost, flexibility, reliability, accessibility, and long-term tradeoffs.
Give advice to a college student who is overwhelmed by coursework, a part-time job, and family responsibilities. Be empathetic and concrete without promising that every problem has an easy fix.
Analyze whether a public library should use a simple facial-recognition system to speed up book checkout. Present benefits, risks, safeguards, and a balanced recommendation.
Write a brief scene about a lighthouse keeper who finds an unexpected message after a storm. Focus on atmosphere and character rather than a twist ending.

A team can choose between finishing a reliable simple version of a project this week or delaying two weeks to add several uncertain features. Explain a decision framework they could use and recommend a default choice.
Summarize the strongest arguments for and against remote work becoming the default for office jobs. Include effects on workers, managers, cities, and new employees.
